subsystems.name: Light-emitting enzyme pair
subsystems.role: the actual light source: a luciferase enzyme oxidises a small molecule (luciferin) and emits a photon.
parts: luciferase gene (typically insect or marine origin)

subsystems.name: Substrate supply
subsystems.role: cells must make their own luciferin continuously, since a permanent implant cannot rely on injections.
parts: transporters to move it into the right cell compartment
ATP and oxygen supply from normal metabolism

subsystems.name: Gene delivery and integration
subsystems.role: inserts the payload into skin-cell DNA so it is inherited as the cells divide.
parts: guide RNA targeting a safe genomic site

subsystems.name: Control circuitry
subsystems.role: makes the glow programmable rather than simply always on.

subsystems.name: Optical path through skin
subsystems.role: much of the light is scattered and absorbed before it leaves the body.
parts: dermal collagen and melanin (the main losses)

subsystems.name: Immune and safety layer
subsystems.role: foreign enzymes are immunogenic and edits must be controllable.

buildSteps.title: Choose and engineer the luciferase
buildSteps.detail: A luminescent enzyme is codon-optimised for human cells and mutated to emit redder light, which travels further through tissue.

buildSteps.title: Build the self-sufficient fuel pathway
buildSteps.detail: Enzymes that build luciferin inside the cell, plus recycling steps, are assembled and tuned so substrate is not the limiting factor.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the genetic cassette
buildSteps.detail: Luciferase, substrate-pathway genes, promoter and control switches are combined into one deliverable construct.

buildSteps.title: Test in cultured skin cells
buildSteps.detail: Fibroblasts or keratinocytes are edited and grown, then measured with a luminometer for brightness, stability and toxicity.

buildSteps.title: Edit and expand patient cells
buildSteps.detail: A small skin biopsy is taken, cells are edited ex vivo and multiplied — the same ex vivo route already used for some skin-graft therapies — or the construct is delivered directly into skin.

buildSteps.title: Graft or deliver
buildSteps.detail: Edited cells are returned as a graft or suspension, or nanoparticles carrying the editor are injected into the dermis.

buildSteps.title: Verify control and safety
buildSteps.detail: Brightness, switching behaviour, immune response and unintended edits are checked over months in animal models first.

buildSteps.title: Establish patterns and longevity
buildSteps.detail: Multiple cell populations with different switches are combined so the glow can form images rather than a uniform sheen.

prerequisites.why: luciferases already work when expressed in mammal and plant cells, though the light produced is very dim.
nearly all demonstrations add the substrate externally; a permanent implant must synthesise and recycle it internally.
ex vivo editing of patient skin cells is feasible today, but safe, durable in-vivo editing of dermal cells is not routine.
bioluminescent emission is orders of magnitude weaker than daylight, so the effect would only be visible in near-darkness.
insect and bacterial proteins provoke immune responses that would extinguish the glow over time.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of glowing plants and animals using added substrate
pathway.unlocks: proof that foreign luminescence genes work inside living tissue.

pathway.milestone: ex vivo edited skin grafts with continuous, simple glow
pathway.unlocks: a first clinical or research use, initially in darkness and mainly for monitoring rather than display.
permanent, controllable glow without injections and with pattern capability.
cosmetic and medical applications — but only if brightness, safety and long-term stability all improve by orders of magnitude.
